title: Handshake's visual world
question: The roll assigned 'The Talking Board'. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll. Whichever you choose, it only lends type, color, density, and one signature move; buttons and inputs stay standard web controls.

options.label: The Talking Board
options.lineage: 1890s American spirit boards: engraved alphabet, YES / NO / GOOD BYE, and a heart-shaped planchette with a glass lens
options.thesis: The decoded text appears letter by letter under the planchette lens; the lens's clarity is the live signal strength.
options.viewport: Top bar: Send/Listen and Acoustic/Simulated as standard tab groups. Main area: the message input with a byte counter (n/140) and the Send button. Below it, one horizontal transmission timeline where each byte's block length is its actual on-air duration. Result area: a received message shows letter by letter under the planchette lens; a failure has the planchette drift to GOOD BYE, with the actual reason in small type (no_sync / crc_mismatch).
options.risk: The most literal reading of 'séance'. If the engraving and wood grain are overdone, it turns into a Halloween costume. The world only lends type, color, and the one lens move; drop it if it starts blocking the controls.

raised.raise: Time is drawn to scale: each byte's block length = its actual 80 ms, so the full 12-second message is visible at a glance.
Every message shows its exact transmission seconds, right-aligned, like a track timing.
At any moment the screen makes only the next action largest: type → send → wait → read.
The shell commits to the walnut ground and bone-white ink; no gray default background.
When a message arrives, it alone owns the result area; nothing competes with it.

options.label: Temple Fortune Slip
options.lineage: Taiwanese temple fortune slips: numbered paper slips, woodblock type, red paper with black ink
options.thesis: Each received message is a numbered fortune slip; a failed decode is 'no answer', like a divination-block toss that refuses to settle.
options.viewport: Same shell as above. The result area becomes a narrow vertical slip: number (No. 7), body text, and transmission seconds; on failure the slip is blank with the reason stamped in.
options.risk: Highly local: judges may not know the ritual, so a one-line explanation is needed. The vertical slip constrains Latin-text layout.

options.label: Darkroom Exposure Record
options.lineage: darkroom enlarging records: an 11-step gray scale with hatching
options.thesis: Signal strength mapped onto a fixed 11-step tonal scale: −25 to 40 dB, each step one gray value.
options.viewport: The SNR slider becomes an 11-step tonal ramp; the received text sits on the light region, and as signal fades the hatching gets denser.
options.case: Holds product clarity (signal strength visible at a glance), but loses audience identification: it reads as a darkroom tool, not a séance.
options.risk: The strongest functionally but the coldest; it nearly drops the séance story steering asks for.

options.label: Metro Tiles
options.case: Loses on both axes: no séance, and tiles don't fit a send/receive flow.
options.kept: Total color commitment: the shell has no gray default.

options.label: Vertical Video Feed
options.case: Loses on both axes: messages aren't media.
options.kept: When something arrives it alone owns the stage.

options.label: Cassette J-Card
options.kept: Exact running time for each item, right-aligned.

options.label: Airport Wayfinding
options.kept: Show only the next decision, at the largest size.

canonCard.label: Standard utility tool
canonCard.thesis: A clean, plain utility like a web audio tool: white background, sans-serif, one blue accent, done.
canonCard.viewport: Standard form: input, send button, result card.
canonCard.risk: Drops the séance story steering requires.
